title: Quench dynamics in nonreciprocal Aubry-André-Harper model
authors: Zhiyu Pei, Yongxu Fu, Gao Xianlong
abstract: The critical phase of a non-Hermitian quasicrystal can support stronger transport than its surrounding delocalized phase. We demonstrate this anomalous behavior in the one-dimensional nonreciprocal Aubry-André-Harper model through a combined study of dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) and wavepacket diffusion. Using a parity-sorted energy-spectrum classification that directly encodes the generalized $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, we find that DQPTs in this system are energy-resolved, in contrast to the energy-independent DQPTs of Hermitian quasicrystals. The energy-resolved features are most pronounced when the initial and final Hamiltonians belong to different phases (localized or extended), and they are tied to the even-odd index structure of the spectrum, which we exploit to organize the quench-dynamical landscape. For wavepacket dynamics after a single-site quench, the diffusion exponent $β$, extracted from the long-time power-law scaling of the root-mean-square displacement $σ(τ)$, partitions the phase diagram into four distinct regimes. In the Hermitian limit the extended phase is ballistic ($β=1$), the critical phase is normally diffusive ($β=0.5$), and the localized phase yields $β\to 0$. Nonreciprocity reverses this hierarchy: the extended phase becomes normally diffusive, while the critical phase turns ballistic. We trace the anomalous $β=1$ at criticality to the self-similar multifractal structure of the critical eigenstates, whose nodal positions are organized by the golden ratio. A finite-size scaling ansatz built on the wave-front propagation yields $σ(τ)\proptoτ$. The parity-resolved DQPTs and the $β$-phase diagram establish two complementary dynamical diagnostics of nonreciprocal quasicrystals, in which nonreciprocity promotes transport at the critical point and suppresses it in the delocalized phase.
summary: This work analyzes quench dynamics in the nonreciprocal Aubry-André-Harper model, revealing that nonreciprocity dramatically alters transport behavior. By studying wavepacket diffusion and DQPTs, the authors show that the critical phase becomes ballistic, a reversal of the behavior seen in standard Hermitian systems. This establishes nonreciprocity as a key mechanism controlling quantum transport in quasiperiodic lattices.
main_problem: The study investigates how nonreciprocity affects quench dynamics and Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions (DQPTs) in a quasiperiodic lattice.
main_result: Nonreciprocity reverses the transport hierarchy, causing the critical phase to become ballistic ($ eta=1$) while suppressing transport in the delocalized phase.
method: The analysis combines studying the Loschmidt echo for DQPTs with measuring the long-time power-law scaling exponent ($ eta$) of the wavepacket root-mean-square displacement.
model_or_system:
The system is the one-dimensional nonreciprocal Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) model, characterized by non-Hermitian hopping terms ($t_R 
eq t_L$) and a quasiperiodic potential.
key_observables: Diffusion exponent $ eta$ ($\sigma(	au) \propto 	au^ eta$), Loschmidt echo $L(	au)$, and the energy-resolved nature of DQPTs.
important_parameters: Nonreciprocity parameter $\delta$, quasiperiodic potential strength $\lambda$, and the golden ratio $\alpha$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on parity-sorted energy-spectrum classification to organize the quench landscape, and perturbative methods are used for some derivations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the complex energy spectrum, the phase diagram using MIPR, and comparisons between perturbative solutions and numerical quench dynamics for even/odd indexed states.
paper_structure: The paper develops two complementary diagnostics: energy-resolved DQPTs using the Loschmidt echo, and the $ eta$-phase diagram derived from wavepacket diffusion, both highlighting the unique role of nonreciprocity.
why_interesting: The findings provide a detailed, quantitative understanding of how breaking time-reversal symmetry (nonreciprocity) fundamentally alters transport properties at critical points in quasiperiodic systems, which is highly relevant for engineered quantum materials.

(b) Phase diagram of the mean inverse participation ra- tio (MIPR) in the λ–δ plane for N = 233, where the color encodes the localization strength. (c) Parity-sorting scheme: in the extended phase (λ < 2 + 2δ), eigenstates are ordered by ReE in ascending order, then by ImE for degenerate real parts; even (odd) indices correspond to positive (negative) imaginary parts.

FIG. 2: Time-resolved quench dynamics between the strongly localized and deeply extended limits. (a)-(c) Quenches from the deeply extended state (λ = 0) to the strongly localized one (λ →∞). (d)-(f) Quenches from the strongly localized to the deeply extended state. (a), (b) Analytical results for Loschmidt echo L(τ) and the corresponding rate function g(τ) at δ = 0.2. (c), (f) Numerical L(τ) from the full spectrum of the initial Hamiltonian, demonstrating the energy-independent behavior for N = 233.

FIG. 5: Diffusion dynamics in the nonreciprocal AAH model. (a) Phase diagram of the diffusion exponent β in the λ-δ plane, colored by β, which divides the phase di- agram into four distinct regions: (I) localized phase, (II) critical phase, (III) reciprocal diffusive phase, and (IV) nonreciprocal diffusive phase. (b) Wavepacket spreading σ(τ) at δ = 0.5, for representative λ values along the dashed line in (a): λ = 0 (deeply diffusive phase), λ = 2 (diffusive phase), λ = 3 (critical phase), and λ = 4 (lo- calized phase). Insets show the double-logarithmic fits of log σ(τ) versus log τ, where the slope gives the diffusion exponent β. The system size is N = 233.
